ORV
ORV's don't give citizens who want to escape into nature the opportunity to do just that. The ORV catches the eye, it dominates the scene with motion, it kills solitude and stunts the growth and development of outdoor aesthetics. Its root is commercial, not esthetic; hedonistic and pagan, not frugal, disciplined, and sacrificial. In other words, the kinds of philosophies that are pre-requisites to the conservation movement are really not yet understood to the ORV user and manufacturer.
Because of the nature of the ORV itself, we must put restraints on it we will not put on other kinds of recreational devices; sail boats, kayaks, canoes, rowboats, bicycles, skis, snowshoes, ice boats. We believe that ORV's (land, water, air) pose very serious threats to several of our endangered species. By means of the ORV we visualize an ever growing number of ill-informed hunters having access to timber wolves, condors, eagles, antelope, prairie dogs, mountain lions. The consequences, for wildlife, of access by way of ORV use, is ominous for the future of many species.
People are coming into nature hopeful of finding enough quality in the way of the environment to save them the extra expense and time of driving a thousand miles more to a place—like a National Fark where severe restrictions have curtailed ORV activity. Much public land, all over the nation, should be free of the blight of the machine.

114 Vast, intact acreages, not subdued by ORV activity, ought to be available to those who are gentler users of the land.
